problem:
A quadratic equation in the variable $x$ with real coefficients has a root $x=8\text{i}.$ Given that the coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ in the equation is $1,$ find the equation. Write your answer in the form $a{x}^{2}+bx+c=0,$ where $a,$ $b,$ and $c$ are real constants.

{{field-1}}$=0$
worked_solution:
Since the quadratic equation has real coefficients and $x=8\text{i}$ is a root, its conjugate $x=-8\text{i}$ must also be a root. Therefore, using the zero product property, we can write a quadratic equation with the required roots as follows:

$$
(x-8\text{i})(x+8\text{i})=0
$$

Multiplying out the parentheses and simplifying gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{(8\text{i})}^{2} & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-64(-1) & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+64 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
